questions.questionText: Influencing is the process of assigning the tasks developed under the planning function to various individuals or groups within the organization.
questions.explanation: Influencing is the process of guiding and motivating people's activities in appropriate directions. The process of assigning tasks developed under the planning function to various individuals or departments is actually the definition of 'Organizing'.
questions.reference: Answer found on Slide 9 (Organizing) and Slide 10 (Influencing).

questions.questionText: Organizing is also commonly referred to as motivating, leading, directing, or actuating.
questions.explanation: Motivating, leading, directing, or actuating are all alternative terms used to describe the 'Influencing' function of management, not the 'Organizing' function.

questions.questionText: Technical skills involve the ability to apply specialized knowledge and expertise to work-related techniques and procedures.
questions.explanation: According to Robert L. Katz's classic view of management skills, technical skills are explicitly defined as the 'ability to apply specialized knowledge & expertise to work techniques & procedures.'

questions.questionText: Human skills, unlike technical skills, involve the ability to see the organization as a whole.
questions.explanation: The ability to see the organization as a whole is the definition of 'Conceptual Skills'. 'Human Skills' are defined as the ability to work with people.

questions.questionText: Human skills, unlike technical skills, involve the ability to see the organization as a whole.
questions.explanation: The ability to see the organization as a whole is defined as 'Conceptual Skills', whereas 'Human Skills' deal with the ability to work effectively with people.

questions.questionText: The more resources unused during the production process, the more ________ the manager.
questions.explanation: Managerial efficiency refers to the proportion of total organizational resources that contribute to productivity. Therefore, if more resources are unused or wasted (meaning few resources contribute to production), the manager is considered inefficient.
questions.reference: Answer found on Slide 16 and Slide 17.

questions.questionText: A manager is considered efficient and effective if the manager

options.content: does not reach goals and does not waste resources
reaches goals and does not waste resources
does not reach goals and wastes resources

questions.explanation: Effectiveness is defined as making substantial progress toward organizational goals ('doing the right things'), while efficiency is defined as ensuring most resources contribute to production without waste ('doing things right'). Thus, a manager who is both reaches goals and does not waste resources.
questions.reference: Answer found on the matrix on Slide 17.

questions.questionText: In any organization, change-related activities include

options.content: clarifying objectives of jobs in organizations
providing recognition for achievements and contributions

questions.explanation: According to the contemporary view of management skills, 'Task-related' and 'People-related' activities encompass clarifying roles, consulting, providing recognition, and short-term planning. Change-related activities focus on 'modifying organization components', which aligns directly with encouraging innovative thinking and adapting to new methods.
questions.reference: Answer deduced by elimination from the tables on Slide 26 and Slide 28.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true for the management function?

options.content: It reaches goals by working with and through people.
It is a one-time function in an organization.
It is a series of continuing and unrelated activities.
It involves-and concentrates on reaching individual goals.
It does not consider the people aspect of organizations.

questions.explanation: The official definition of management states that it is the continuous process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and utilizing other organizational resources.

questions.questionText: Name one of the basic concepts for smoothly running an organisation.

options.content: None of the options is correct

questions.explanation: The overarching role of management is to guide the organization smoothly towards its goals by effectively utilizing its resources through the execution of its core functions (planning, organizing, influencing, controlling).
questions.reference: Answer supported by the core concepts on Slide 4 and Slide 5.

questions.questionText: ____ resources refer to the machines used during the manufacturing process.
questions.explanation: In the breakdown of organizational resources, 'Assets/Capital' (or Capital resources) specifically refer to the equipment, facilities, and machines that are utilized as inputs in the production process to create goods or services.
questions.reference: Answer supported by Slide 13 and the diagram on Slide 14.

questions.questionText: ____ skills are very important to managers at the lower, middle and top levels.
questions.explanation: According to the classic view charts of management skills, while the need for technical and conceptual skills varies greatly depending on the management level, 'Human Skills' occupy an equally large and consistent segment across top, middle, and supervisory levels.
questions.reference: Answer found on the visual charts on Slide 23 and Slide 24.

questions.questionText: The more resources unused during the production process, the more ____ the manager.
questions.explanation: Managerial efficiency deals directly with the proportion of resources contributing to productivity. A higher proportion of unused or wasted resources means fewer resources are actively contributing to the final product, rendering the manager inefficient.
questions.reference: Answer found on Slide 16 and Slide 17.

questions.questionText: Name one of the basic concepts for smoothly running an organisation.

options.content: None of the options is correct

questions.explanation: Management is the core encompassing concept whose primary role is to smoothly guide the organization towards its goals through the effective use of resources.
questions.reference: Answer supported by the definitions on Slide 4 and Slide 5.

questions.explanation: Basic managerial activities—specifically people-related and task-related skills—encompass supervising (monitoring operations), motivating (which is the core of the 'influencing' function), and stimulating personnel to reach organizational goals efficiently.
questions.reference: Answer supported by the concepts on Slide 10 and Slide 27.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true for the management function?

options.content: It reaches goals by working with and through people.
It is a one-time function in an organization.
It is a series of continuing and unrelated activities.
It involves and concentrates on reaching individual goals.
It does not consider the people aspect of organizations.

questions.explanation: Management is formally defined as the process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and other organizational resources.
